name: Dusty scarlet
lede: Dusty scarlet renders Sohi (蘇比), a traditional Japanese name our library glosses as an "overdyed, refreshed red-brown", for a muted orange-red.

sections.title: A re-dyed red
sections.body:
Our color library gives the source as 蘇比 (Sohi), glossed as an overdyed or refreshed red-brown, from the traditional colors of Japan; no first-recorded date survives in our sources, so when the name entered use is undocumented here [1]. The library separately notes that the ISCC-NBS 1955 centroid block covering this hue groups together English dictionary names such as Nasturtium Red and Russet Orange, the earliest of which, Flammeous, Maerz and Paul date to 1656 [2].

The nearest named color in our graph is [[flame]], at a color distance (ΔE2000) of 3.9, a more vivid shade; the related [[dusty-vermilion]] sits 5.5 away and reads darker [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this orange-red, within six units over at least five percent of the canvas, in 44 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.2 percent, as photographed [4]. It is sharply concentrated in Indian painting, at more than twenty times the archive's overall rate, with Kalighat work, 8 of our 96, running at forty-five times that average and Rajput work close behind [4]. The earliest dated match is Lorenzo Monaco's *Adoration of the Magi* (1420), a floor set by what survives and was photographed, not a first appearance [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings; the match is computed, not a pigment identification [4].
